reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 20 question-paper pages and all 24 scheme PDF pages; detailed allocations checked against the summary on PDF page 7 (printed page 4). Corrupt font-encoded scheme spans were independently transcribed from the rendered originals.
sourceNotes: All ten questions are required. Candidate and offered totals are both 300 marks.
39 independently marked units. Q1(a)(i–iii), Q1(b)(i–iii), Q2(a)(i+ii), Q2(b)(i–iii), Q3(a)(i+ii), Q3(b)(i+ii), Q4(b)(ii–iv), Q8(b)(i+ii) and Q10(b)(i+ii) each retain their single published scale.
Question file LC003BLP100EV.pdf and scheme file LC003BLP000EV.pdf are distinct. Page references are PDF positions.

The PDF scheme has corrupted text mappings in several embedded fonts. The raw extraction is retained alongside explicitly labelled visual transcriptions of affected quotes, keyed by PDF page. The original scheme remains the complete answer source.
Q6 construction and Q7 enlargement tasks need physical measurements. Q7 later parts depend on the unlabelled printed lengths and retain the ruler as well as the original diagram.
The toothpaste stem specifies radius 1.6 cm even though its picture’s arrow spans the width. Preserve the stated radius; the published scheme uses radius 1.6 cm.
2016 10C uses 0,4,7,10; Q10(a)(i) uses 5D, 0,2,3,4,5; Q10(a)(iii) volume is 15C as published.

cards.stem: A bag contains 6 yellow discs, 7 blue discs and 14 red discs.
cards.questionText: (i) What is the total number of discs in the bag? (ii) A disc is picked at random from the bag. What is the probability that the disc is red? (iii) A disc is picked at random from the bag. What is the probability that the disc is yellow or blue?

cards.stem: There are girls and boys in a class. 16 of the students in the class are girls. 9 of these girls play hockey.
cards.questionText: (i) A girl is selected at random from the class. What is the probability that this girl plays hockey? (ii) There are 28 students in the class. The remaining students are boys and 8 of these boys play hockey. A boy is selected at random from the class. What is the probability that this boy plays hockey? (iii) A student is selected at random from the class. What is the probability that this student does not play hockey?

cards.stem: The side of a square is 8 cm.
cards.questionText: (i) Six of these squares have been put together to form the shape shown in the diagram. Find the length of the perimeter of the shape. (ii) The six squares are re-arranged as shown. Find the length of the perimeter of this new shape.

cards.stem: The surface area of a sphere is given by the formula A = 4πr², where r is the radius of the sphere.
cards.questionText: (i) Taking π as 3 and r as 2 cm, estimate the surface area of the sphere in the diagram: A = 4 × 3 × 2² = ___. (ii) The actual radius of the sphere in the diagram is 1·9 cm. Taking π as 3·142 and r as 1·9 cm find a more accurate estimate for the surface area of the sphere. Give your answer correct to one decimal place. (iii) Find the difference between your answers in part b(i) and part b(ii) above.
